messages.subject: constrain connectivity among areas
parts:
Hi again,

I have built a matrix of approximate connectivity between the areas as fractions, with 1 .000 being the maximum connectivity for adjacent locations and 0.001 being the minimum connectivity for distant locations or locations with putative barriers between them.
I uncommented the BioGeoBEARS_run_object$distsfn = "distances_matrix.txt"

> BioGeoBEARS_run_object = readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
[1] "AR\tAZ\tBS\tBE\tFA\tAB\tVC"

[1] "END"

>$BioGeoBEARS_model_object
$list_of_distances_mats[[1]]
     AR    AZ    BS    BE    FA    AB    VC
1    NA 1.000 0.010 0.010 0.001 0.001 0.010
2 1.000    NA 0.100 0.100 0.001 0.001 0.010
3 0.010 0.100    NA 0.001 0.001 0.001 0.001

Thanks,
Rita

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] constrain connectivity among areas
parts:
On my phone but:

1. Use the manual dispersal multipliers for what you are doing

2. To get distances to work you would have to set the parameter x to be free or set it to a value less than zero. And you would want distances instead of multipliers, although there are ways it could work the other way by reversing the sign of X but it's best to keep it simple

3. The phylowiki main page for biogeobears now has a long section explaining the different matrices, it's good to get clear on what does what. Cheers! Nick

Hi!
So I am trying actually to use manual dispersal multipliers, as I think the dispersal between sites in not a function of geographic distance due to dispersal barriers. So a manual dispersal multipliers will allow me to ascribe probabilities of dispersal.
I have check the google groups previous message and you say to uncomment this
#BioGeoBEARS_run_object$dispersal_multipliers_fn = "manual_dispersal_multipliers.txt"
and to turn on "w" by editing the BioGeoBEARS_model_object parameters table:
# Add w as a free parameter
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["w","type"] = "free"
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["w","init"] = 0
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["w","est"] = 0
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["w","min"] = 0
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["w","max"] = 3

So given a manual_dispersal_multipliers.txt file and these commands, will the model work? On running the DEC+J adding the previous commands will get the DEC+J+W model? I am asking this because of the 
dstart = restart = resDEC$outputs@params_table["e","est"] etc commands, I was thinking if something similar is needed for w?

Thanks,
Rita

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] constrain connectivity among areas
parts:
On plane- on my way to Evolution 2016 In Austin, I will be doing a BioGeoBEARS help session at iEvoBio there by the way... 

Re: your question, dstart etc are just ways to use the d estimate from eg DEC for the starting point of eg DEC+J. This can help you check ML optimization - please read PhyloWiki for advice on double-checking ML optimization. But it's not required.

For w, the fixed default is w=1 so run a model with w fixed to 1 (eg regular DEC+J) and another with w free, eg DEC+J+w. 

Note for everyone : understanding the concepts of nested models and the concept that adding a free parameter should always equal or improve the likelihood (if it doesn't then you have optimization problems) is really a key requirement for doing model comparison in BGB or any other software. I have put a lot of tips on the phylowiki since I see these basics misunderstood a lot, sometimes even by reviewers...  Cheers! Nick
